'''Mary Eleanor Clark''' (April 28, 1927, [[San Francisco]] – December 11, 2019, [[Veneta, Oregon|Veneta]], Oregon) was an American biologist. She was named the first National Professor of the Year by the Council for Advancement and Support of Education.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1981-10-26 |title=Here's what the professor of the year has to say |work=Christian Science Monitor |url=https://www.csmonitor.com/1981/1026/102605.html |access-date=2022-03-10 |issn=0882-7729}}</ref> In 1978, she was named a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Historic Fellows {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic |access-date=2022-03-16 |website=www.aaas.org |language=en}}</ref>

== Life ==
She was raised in San Francisco by her father, Raymond F. Clark and mother, Norton J. Clark.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 13, 2003 |title=CLARK, Mary E. |url=https://www.sfgate.com/news/article/clark-mary-e-2557552.php |access-date=July 16, 2024 |website=San Francisco Gate}}</ref> At the [[University of California, Berkeley|University California, Berkeley]], Clark earned her Bachelor in Biochemistry, 1949; Master of Arts in Biology, 1951; and Doctor of Philosophy, 1960. She went on to become a biology professor at [[San Diego State University]], [[George Mason University]], [[Denison University]] and the [[University of Montevallo]]. She was named National Professor of Year by the Council Advancement and Support Education, 1981.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Mary Eleanor Clark (née Lawrence) |url=https://www.gatheringus.com/memorial/mary-eleanor-clark-nee-lawrence/2343 |access-date=2022-03-10 |website=GatheringUs |language=en}}</ref>

In addition, she was an accomplished artist and musician and was known for her love of the outdoors.<ref name=":0" />
